publish_help.bimi: Writes default._bimi.<domain>: the record that tells mailbox providers where your logo (and certificate) is. Mailfilter hosts both files itself. You can undo this in the change log.
publish_help.spf: Your current SPF value stays as it is; Mailfilter only adds itself. Nothing else changes.
publish_help.spf_value: This replaces the domain's SPF record with the generated value.
publish_help.dkim: Publishes the public key Mailfilter signs outbound mail with.
publish_help.dmarc: This sets the domain's DMARC record to the value shown.
publish_help.server_spf: The shared record that lists all Mailfilter addresses. Domains include this name.
publish_help.mx: Cloudflare will get exactly these MX records. New records are added before old ones are removed, so mail keeps flowing. You can undo this in the change log.
publish_help.mta_sts: mta-sts.<domain> points to Mailfilter, which serves the policy file. The TXT record tells senders which policy version is current.
publish_help.tls_rpt: Senders that have trouble setting up an encrypted connection send a daily report to this address.
publish_help.tlsa: The TLSA record holds the fingerprint of Mailfilter's key. Certificate renewals keep the same key, so the record stays valid.
publish_help.dmarc_rua: Adds Mailfilter's report address to the domain's DMARC record. Everything else in the record stays. Without a record, a new one starts at p=none, which blocks nothing.
publish_help.dmarc_policy: Changes only p= in the DMARC record (and removes pct=, so the policy applies to all mail). Everything else stays. You can undo this in the change log.
publish_help.dmarc_auth: One record on Mailfilter's own name that allows every domain, also customer domains added later, to send its DMARC reports here (RFC 7489, section 7.1).

tls.help: These records make sure mail to your domains is always sent encrypted, so nobody on the way can force an unencrypted connection.
tls.sts_help: Tells senders that mail for this domain must be delivered over a verified TLS connection to the listed servers. Mailfilter serves the policy itself on mta-sts.<domain> and gets a certificate for it automatically. Start in test mode and switch to enforce once the MX points to {{host}}.
tls.mode_testing_help: Senders report problems (TLS-RPT) but still deliver.
tls.mode_enforce_help: Senders only deliver over a verified encrypted connection to the listed MX servers.
tls.mode_none_help: Use this to switch MTA-STS off: senders forget the policy.
tls.mx_hint: Every MX of the domain must be listed. *.example.com covers one level.
tls.rpt_help: Senders send a daily report about failed encrypted connections to this address. Useful together with MTA-STS in test mode.
tls.dane_help: A TLSA record with the fingerprint of the key of {{host}}. Senders that support DANE then only deliver encrypted to exactly this server. It only works when DNSSEC is on.
tls.dnssec_how: Turn on DNSSEC in Cloudflare: open the domain, go to DNS > Settings and click Enable DNSSEC. If the domain is not registered with Cloudflare, add the DS record that Cloudflare shows at your registrar.

help.intro: Every domain signs its mail with a DKIM key. Mailfilter replaces each key after {{months}} months: it makes a new key, publishes its record, switches over when DNS shows it, and removes the old record {{days}} days later. Mail keeps passing DKIM the whole time.
help.publish_auto: The new record has been put in Cloudflare. As soon as the domain's own name servers show it, the next step starts.
help.publish_manual: This domain is not in Cloudflare. Add the record below at your DNS provider; Mailfilter checks every six hours (or press Check now) and continues by itself.
help.wait: The new record is in DNS. To let caches catch up, the new key starts signing after {{hours}} hours, around {{date}}.
help.overlap_auto: The new key signs now. The old record ({{old}}) stays in DNS until {{date}} for mail that was signed just before the switch; then Mailfilter removes it from Cloudflare.
help.overlap_manual: The new key signs now. The old record ({{old}}) is still needed until {{date}}; after that you can remove it at your DNS provider.

dkimrot.enabled_d: Replace DKIM keys on a fixed schedule. A key that is used for years is more likely to leak or be cracked.
dkimrot.interval_d: Age of a key before it is replaced. Six months is common practice.
dkimrot.wait_d: Time between the new record appearing in DNS and the new key signing, so every DNS cache has it.
dkimrot.overlap_d: Mail is sometimes checked days after it was sent (forwarding, mailing lists). Until then the old record must stay.
dkimrot.manual_dns_d: Start rotations for domains whose DNS is not in Cloudflare too. You then publish the new record yourself; until you do, the old key keeps signing.
dkimrot.run_done: Checked; rotations are up to date
dkimrot.rotate_confirm: Make a new DKIM key for {{domain}} now? The current key keeps signing until the new record is in DNS.
dkimrot.cancel_confirm: Cancel this rotation? The new key is deleted and the current key keeps signing.
dkimrot.not_leader: This server is in a cluster. Key rotation is done by {{node}}; the new keys reach this server through the cluster sync.
dkimrot.no_cloudflare: No Cloudflare token is set, so new records cannot be published automatically. Rotation only starts for domains you rotate by hand, or with "Also domains outside Cloudflare" switched on.

bimi.help: With BIMI your logo appears next to your mail in Gmail, Apple Mail, Yahoo and others. Mailfilter checks what is still missing, converts your logo, hosts the files and publishes the DNS record.

ready.title: What is needed
ready.dmarc_help: Mail apps only trust the logo when DMARC blocks fake mail.
ready.logo_help: A square SVG in a special, safe format. Mailfilter can convert most logos.
ready.record_help: default._bimi.<domain> tells mail apps where the logo is.
ready.cert_help: Only needed for Gmail and Apple Mail. You buy it from DigiCert, Sectigo, GlobalSign or Entrust.
ready.level_full_help: Everything is in place. Mail apps can take a few days before they show the logo.
ready.level_basic_help: Yahoo, Fastmail and others can show the logo now. Gmail and Apple Mail also need a VMC or CMC.
ready.level_none_help: Work through the steps above. Steps 1 to 3 are free.

dmarc.title: DMARC
dmarc.help: BIMI requires DMARC with p=quarantine or p=reject for all mail (pct=100). Without that, mail apps ignore your logo.
dmarc.careful: Only switch DMARC on when all real senders (website, newsletter, invoicing) pass. Check the DMARC reports page first.

p.dmarc_invalid: The DMARC record has an error.
p.dmarc_not_enforced: The policy is {{value}}; it must be quarantine or reject.
p.dmarc_pct: Only {{value}}% of the mail falls under the policy; it must be 100%.
p.dmarc_sp_none: Subdomains have sp=none; remove it or set it to quarantine or reject.

logo.title: Logo
logo.help: Upload your logo as SVG. Use a square version with a solid background colour: mail apps show it in a circle. Mailfilter checks the file and can convert an ordinary SVG to SVG Tiny PS.
logo.name: Name in the logo
logo.remove_confirm: Remove the logo? If the BIMI record is published, mail apps then show no logo.
logo.valid: This logo is valid SVG Tiny PS.
logo.converted_ok: Converted. Check the preview: does the logo still look right?
logo.invalid: This logo does not meet SVG Tiny PS yet:
logo.title_hint: Goes into the logo as its title. Empty: the domain name.

svg.too_large: The file is {{value}} KB; at most 32 KB is allowed.
svg.version: version="1.2" is missing on the svg element.
svg.base_profile: baseProfile="tiny-ps" is missing on the svg element.
svg.root_xy: The svg element may not have x or y.
svg.no_title: A <title> with the company name is missing.
svg.external_ref: Refers to files elsewhere on the internet.
svg.style_attr: Uses style="..." instead of plain attributes.

change.inlined_css: CSS styles turned into plain attributes
change.dropped_css: CSS that SVG Tiny does not support removed
change.made_square: Made square (space added at the sides; a solid background looks better)

cert.title: Mark certificate (VMC or CMC)
cert.help: Gmail and Apple Mail only show your logo with a mark certificate. It proves the logo belongs to you and contains the logo itself. Upload the .pem file you get from the issuer (with the full chain).
cert.vmc: VMC (Verified Mark Certificate): for a registered trademark of your logo. Gmail shows a blue check mark.
cert.cmc: CMC (Common Mark Certificate): no trademark needed; the logo must have been on your website for at least a year. Gmail shows the logo without a check mark.
cert.remove_confirm: Remove the certificate? Gmail and Apple Mail then stop showing the logo.
cert.logo_used: The logo from the certificate is now used

certp.not_yet_valid: The certificate is not valid yet.
certp.expires_soon: Expires in {{value}} days; renew it in time.
certp.no_bimi_eku: This is not a BIMI certificate (the BIMI usage is missing).
certp.domain_mismatch: The certificate is not for this domain (it is for {{value}}).
certp.logo_differs: The logo in the certificate differs from the uploaded logo. Gmail needs them to be the same: use the logo from the certificate.
certp.no_chain: Only the certificate itself, without the intermediate certificate. Download the full chain from the issuer.

record.title: BIMI record
record.help: This DNS record tells mail apps where your logo and certificate are. Mailfilter serves both files over HTTPS.
record.need_logo: Upload a valid logo first; then the record is ready.

dmarc.title: DMARC reports
dmarc.sub_admin: Who sends mail as your domains, whether it passes DMARC, and the next safe step towards p=reject.
dmarc.sub_customer: Who sends mail as your domains and whether it passes DMARC.
dmarc.k_pass_sub: DKIM or SPF aligned with the From domain
dmarc.k_fail_sub: forged, or a sender that is not set up yet
dmarc.upload_error_one: This is not a DMARC report Mailfilter can read
dmarc.upload_error_other: This is not a DMARC report Mailfilter can read
dmarc.upload_ignored_one: No DMARC report found in this file
dmarc.upload_ignored_other: No DMARC report found in this file
dmarc.rua_help: Mail providers such as Google and Microsoft send a daily report to the rua address in a domain's DMARC record. Mailfilter receives them at this address and shows them here. Use "Receive reports" on a domain to add it via Cloudflare; other addresses in the record stay.
dmarc.auth_manual: Add a TXT record {{name}} with value v=DMARC1.
dmarc.setup_incomplete: Not everything is in place yet. Without the "allowed" record, providers do not send reports about customer domains to this address.
dmarc.nothing_received: No report mail received yet. Reports usually arrive within 24 to 48 hours after the rua address is published.
dmarc.road_none: Monitor only: collect reports, nothing is blocked
dmarc.road_quarantine: Mail that fails goes to spam
dmarc.road_reject: Mail that fails is refused: full protection

advice.record_invalid: The DMARC record has a syntax error
advice.record_invalid_sub: Receivers ignore a broken record, so the domain has no protection. Fix it in the DNS toolbox (DMARC generator).
advice.no_record: This domain has no DMARC record
advice.no_record_sub: Start with p=none and the report address {{rua}}: nothing is blocked yet, and you will see who sends mail as {{domain}}.
advice.no_rua: Reports for this domain do not come to Mailfilter yet
advice.no_rua_sub: Add {{rua}} to the rua= tag of the DMARC record. Other report addresses stay.
advice.waiting_reports_sub: Providers send reports once a day, so the first ones usually arrive within 24 to 48 hours.
advice.collecting_sub: Everything looks fine so far. Wait until there are reports for at least {{need}} days, so that senders that only mail now and then show up too.
advice.fix_senders_sub: They send real mail as this domain but fail DMARC. Give them a DKIM key for this domain, or add them to SPF with a matching envelope sender. Tightening the policy now would send their mail to spam.
advice.ready_quarantine_sub: All real senders pass DMARC. Mail that fails, which is most likely forged, will go to the spam folder. Keep an eye on this page for two weeks after the change.
advice.raise_pct: The policy covers only {{pct}}% of the mail
advice.raise_pct_sub: The rest is treated as p=none. All real senders pass, so the policy can apply to all mail.
advice.quarantine_wait_sub: No real sender has problems. After {{need}} days at quarantine, the next step is p=reject.
advice.ready_reject_sub: Real senders have passed DMARC for at least two weeks at quarantine. With p=reject, receivers refuse forged mail outright.
advice.done_sp: p=reject is active, subdomains still use sp={{sp}}
advice.done_sp_sub: Mail as {{domain}} is fully protected. Mail as a subdomain is not yet; change sp= when no subdomain sends mail of its own.
advice.done_sub: Receivers refuse mail that pretends to come from {{domain}}. Mailfilter keeps reading the reports, so a new sender that is not set up shows up here.

dmarc.manual_admin: Connect Cloudflare in the DNS toolbox to make this change with one click, or change the record at your DNS provider.
dmarc.manual_customer: Ask your administrator to make this change.
dmarc.record_dns_error: DNS did not answer; the advice uses the newest report.

verdict_help.ok: All mail from this sender passes DMARC.
verdict_help.minor: Almost all mail passes. The few failures are usually forwarded mail or mailing lists, where SPF cannot pass.
verdict_help.fix: This sender sends real mail as your domain but it fails DMARC. Set up DKIM for your domain at this service, or add it to SPF.
verdict_help.suspect: Unknown sender whose mail always fails. This is most likely spoofing; a stricter policy blocks it. If you do know this sender, set it up with DKIM or SPF.

dmarc.domain_sub: Based on the reports of the mail providers that received mail from this domain.
dmarc.k_spf_sub: envelope sender in this domain passes SPF
dmarc.chart_note: Per day of the report period (UTC). Reports for yesterday usually arrive today.
dmarc.no_data_rua: No reports yet. Add the report address first (see Next step).

gateway.apply_failed: Not saved: the mail server check "{{step}}" failed, so nothing was changed.
gateway.applied: Saved and active on the mail server
gateway.last_ok: Mail server configuration is up to date (last change {{at}}).
gateway.last_failed: The last change on {{at}} was refused by the mail server; the previous configuration is still active.
gateway.never_applied: The configuration has not been written from the web interface yet.

domains.title: Domains
domains.sub: Domains the Mailfilter accepts mail for, and the mail server that receives the clean mail.
domains.sub_customer: Your domains and where their mail is delivered.
domains.empty: No domains yet. Add the first domain to start filtering.
domains.name: Domain
domains.not_configured_hint: This domain exists for users, but mail for it is not accepted yet. Enter its mail server to start.
domains.destinations_hint: Clean mail goes to the main server; backup servers are used when it cannot be reached.
domains.mx_hint: Look up the MX records of this host name instead of connecting to it directly.
domains.tls_hint: Required: never deliver without TLS. Verified: also check the certificate.
domains.verify_hint: Ask the mail server before accepting a message, so mail for unknown addresses is refused at the door (no backscatter).
domains.concurrency_hint: How many messages are delivered at the same time. Empty: default.
domains.rate_delay_hint: For mail servers that cannot keep up. Delivers one message at a time.
domains.outbound_hint: Mail sent out from this domain via the Mailfilter. Empty: the default from Throttling.
domains.enabled: Accept and deliver mail for this domain
domains.delete_confirm: Delete {{name}}? Mail for this domain is refused from then on.
domains.tls_sub: Require TLS for specific receiving domains
domains.tls_empty: No rules; encryption is used when available.

relay.title: Relay access
relay.sub: Servers (for example web servers) that may send mail out through the Mailfilter. Their mail is still checked for spam and viruses. A server linked to a customer domain may only send as that customer's own domains.
relay.sub_customer: Your servers that may send mail out through the Mailfilter. They may only send mail from your own domains.
relay.hint: Use one IP address for one server, or a network such as 203.0.113.0/28. IPv4 and IPv6 both work.
relay.confirm_broad: Yes, this large network is really ours
relay.ports_sub: Extra ports next to 587 and 465, e.g. for old software

throttling.title: Throttling
throttling.sub: Limits for mail going out through the Mailfilter, so one hacked web server or account cannot send thousands of spam messages.
throttling.defaults_sub: Apply unless a domain has its own limit
throttling.relay_ip_per_minute_hint: Messages one relay IP may send per minute.
throttling.relay_ip_per_hour_hint: Messages one relay IP may send per hour.
throttling.domain_per_hour_hint: Set a different limit per domain under Domains.
throttling.domain_per_day_hint: Set a different limit per domain under Domains.
throttling.user_per_hour_hint: Messages one SMTP login may send per hour.
throttling.concurrency_hint: Default for each domain's own delivery queue.
throttling.destinations_sub: Big providers block senders that go too fast
throttling.domain_limits_hint: Limits for your own domains are set per domain under Domains.

jobs.reconnecting: The web interface is restarting. This page reconnects by itself.
jobs.done_update: Update finished. The page reloads in a moment.
jobs.done_restore: Restore finished. Everything is running again.
jobs.failed_update: Update failed. The previous version was put back.

steps.backup_files: Saving files (settings, DKIM keys, certificates, quarantine)
steps.restore_safety: Making a safety backup of the current state
steps.update_rollback: Update failed, putting the previous version back
steps.remote_failed: Copy to the remote location failed: {{error}}

backups.title: Backups
backups.sub: Local backups of all settings, DKIM keys, certificates, quarantine, the database and the spam filter's learning data.
backups.empty: No backups yet. The first one is made tonight, or press Full backup now.
backups.verify: Check that the backup is complete
backups.delete: Delete this full backup and its incrementals
backups.delete_confirm: Delete the full backup of {{when}} and all incremental backups that build on it?
backups.nightly_d: Every night; a full backup every {{days}} days, incremental in between.
backups.keep_d: Older ones are removed together with their incrementals.
backups.comp_files_d: settings, lists, passwords, DKIM keys, certificates, quarantined mail

remote.title: Remote copy
remote.settings_sub: After every backup the new full or incremental backup is copied to this server.
remote.off_d: Keep a copy of every backup on another server over SCP, FTPS or FTP, so you can restore after losing this server.
remote.on_d_one: Keeps 1 full backup with its incrementals.
remote.on_d_other: Keeps {{count}} full backups with their incrementals.
remote.empty: No backups on the remote location yet.
remote.enabled_d: Runs after every backup. A failed copy is reported but keeps the local backup.
remote.ftp_warn: Plain FTP sends the password unencrypted. Use it only inside a trusted network; the backup files themselves are still encrypted.
remote.password_keep: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
remote.path_d: Relative to the login folder, or starting with / for an absolute path. Created if needed.
remote.keep_d: Older ones are removed from the remote location together with their incrementals.
remote.verify_tls_d: Switch off only for a server with a self-signed certificate.
remote.ssh_key_d: Add this public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of user {{user}} on the backup server. No password is stored.
remote.ssh_key_after_save: A key pair is made when you save.
remote.forget_confirm: Forget the stored fingerprint? The next connection test stores the server's current one. Only do this if the server really got a new key.
remote.encrypt: Encrypt backups before they leave this server
remote.encrypt_d: AES-256 with a passphrase. Only dates, sizes and checksums stay readable.
remote.encrypt_warn: Backups contain passwords and DKIM keys. Without encryption anyone with access to the remote server can read them.
remote.passphrase_d: Store the passphrase in your password manager. You need it to restore these backups on a new server; without it they cannot be opened.
remote.passphrase_hint: At least 12 characters. Leave empty to keep the current one (a random one is made on first save). Backups already copied keep their old passphrase.
remote.test_ok: Connection works: logged in, uploaded and removed a test file.
remote.restore_d: The backup and the backups it builds on are downloaded and checked first. On a new server, set up the remote location with the same passphrase before restoring.

backups.restore_warn: Restoring replaces the current settings and data with those from this backup. Mail services stop for a moment; incoming mail waits at the sender and is delivered afterwards.
backups.restore_chain_one: This incremental backup builds on the full backup and 1 earlier step; all are replayed in order.
backups.restore_chain_other: This incremental backup builds on the full backup and {{count}} earlier steps; all are replayed in order.
backups.safety: Make a safety backup of the current state first (recommended)
backups.remote_later: Copying backups to FTP, FTPS or SCP comes in a later version.

smtp.title: E-mail sending
smtp.sub: How Mailfilter sends its own messages: alerts, quarantine reports, password notices and backup reports.
smtp.mode_local_d: Uses the gateway's own Postfix. Messages are DKIM-signed like all other mail. Recommended.
smtp.mode_smtp_d: For example Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or your own mail server.
smtp.username_d: Leave empty if the server does not need a login.
smtp.password_keep: A password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
smtp.insecure: Without encryption or certificate check, passwords and mail can be read or changed on the way.
smtp.test_d: Uses the settings in the form, also before saving.
smtp.modern_tls: TLS 1.2 or newer, with certificate checks, through STARTTLS or direct TLS
smtp.modern_auth: SMTP AUTH; the password is stored encrypted
smtp.modern_headers: Date, Message-ID and Auto-Submitted headers, so autoresponders do not reply
smtp.modern_local: Default route through the gateway itself, with DKIM signing

pmg.title: Import from Proxmox Mail Gateway
pmg.sub: Take over domains, relay access, allow and block lists and DKIM from your PMG. You see everything first and choose what to import.
pmg.how1: Open the PMG web interface and go to Administration → Backup/Restore.
pmg.drop: Drop the backup file here or click to choose

help.domains: Domains Mailfilter accepts mail for, with the server mail is delivered to.
help.relay_networks: IP addresses and networks that may send mail out through Mailfilter (PMG: Trusted Networks).
help.address_routes: Single addresses or other domains that go to their own server.
help.tls_policies: Destinations that require an encrypted connection.
help.lists: Senders that are always let through (allow) or always refused (block).

pmg.confirm: Import {{count}} items into this Mailfilter? Postfix and Rspamd are checked before anything goes live.
pmg.safe: Everything is checked first; if a check fails, nothing is changed.
pmg.failed: Import not done, nothing was changed

rules.title: Custom rules
rules.sub: Extra filter rules you can switch on and off, for all domains or per domain.
rules.intro: Every rule explains what it does. A rule with a spam score adds that score; from 8 a message goes to quarantine, from 15 it is refused. Changes are checked by Rspamd and take effect straight away; if Rspamd does not accept a change, nothing is changed.
rules.intro_customer: These rules are set by your administrator. Per domain you can choose to follow that setting or switch a rule on or off for your own domains.

group_sub.newsletter: Recognise newsletters and catch the ones that break the rules
group_sub.phishing: Catch messages that pretend to come from you or your colleagues
group_sub.attachments: Stop dangerous files before they reach anyone
group_sub.arc: Keep forwarded mail working with DMARC

rules.per_domain_hint: Default follows the switch above. For a message to several domains, the rule applies when it is on for at least one of them.
rules.symbol: Shows in the mail trace as
rules.admin_only: Only an administrator can change this
rules.list_hint: One per line, or separated by commas
rules.global_only: This rule applies to all domains at once.

holds.why_spam: {{spam}} of {{total}} messages in {{minutes}} minutes were spam
holds.held_count_one: {{count}} message is on hold, nothing has been lost or sent.
holds.held_count_other: {{count}} messages are on hold, nothing has been lost or sent.
holds.ask_admin: Ask your administrator to release it
holds.release_text: Only do this once the website, server or mailbox is safe again (password changed, hole fixed). New mail goes out normally again. What should happen to the mail that was held?
holds.pause_confirm: Pause {{value}}? Its mail is kept on hold until you release it.

protection.title: Automatic protection
protection.sub: Every minute Mailfilter checks the outgoing mail of each sending server and SMTP account. A sender that suddenly sends spam or far more mail than usual (a hacked website or mailbox) is paused: its mail is kept on hold, administrators get an e-mail, and you release it under Relay access.
protection.enabled_hint: Off: nothing is paused automatically (you can still pause by hand).
protection.window_minutes_hint: How many minutes of mail are checked each time.
protection.spam_min: Spam: at least this many messages
protection.spam_min_hint: A few spam messages are normal; a hacked sender sends many.
protection.spam_percent_hint: And at least this share of all its mail must be spam.
protection.volume_min: Volume: at least this many messages
protection.volume_min_hint: Small senders are never paused for volume.
protection.volume_factor_hint: Compared with the average of the last 7 days.
protection.quiet_hours_hint: So a sender you just released is not paused again straight away.
protection.exempt_hint: IP addresses or SMTP accounts, one per line.
protection.notify_hint: Extra e-mail addresses for this alert, one per line, on top of the recipients under Notifications.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.sub: Get alerts by e-mail, Telegram or webhook when something needs your attention, also when nobody is looking at this screen.
notify.ch_email_d: Alerts by e-mail, sent with the settings under E-mail sending.
notify.ch_telegram_d: Alerts as a Telegram message from your own bot, in a private chat or a group.
notify.ch_webhook_d: Alerts as an HTTP POST to your own system, Slack, Mattermost or Discord.
notify.email_to_d: One address per line. Empty = all administrators ({{list}}).
notify.email_via: Mail is sent with the settings under
notify.tg_step1: In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot and copy the token you get.
notify.tg_step2: Send your new bot a message (or add it to a group and send a message there).
notify.tg_step3: Paste the token below and click "Find chat", then pick your chat.
notify.tg_chat_d: Group IDs start with a minus sign.
notify.tg_none: No chats found. Send the bot a message first, then try again.
notify.secret_keep: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
notify.wh_format_json_d: Fields: event, type, code, level, title, message, link, params, time.
notify.wh_format_slack_d: Use an incoming webhook URL from Slack or Mattermost.
notify.wh_format_discord_d: Use a webhook URL from the Discord channel settings.
notify.wh_secret_d: Optional. Each request then gets X-Mailfilter-Signature: sha256=HMAC(secret, timestamp + "." + body).
notify.test_ok: Test sent. Check that it arrived.
notify.type_services_d: Postfix, Rspamd, ClamAV, the web interface or another part stops (after 3 minutes).
notify.type_queue_d: Many messages are waiting because they cannot be delivered.
notify.type_blacklist_d: One of the server's addresses appears on a blocklist.
notify.type_certificate_d: The Let's Encrypt certificate is not renewed in time.
notify.type_abuse_d: A server or account was paused because it suddenly sent spam or a flood of mail.
notify.type_backup_d: A backup, remote copy, restore or update failed, or there has been no successful backup for a while.
notify.language_d: Telegram and webhook messages and e-mails use this language.
notify.repeat_d: Send the alert again while the problem lasts. 0 = only once.
notify.resolved_d: Send a short message when a problem is over.
notify.active_none: No problems. Everything the checker looks at is fine.

lists.title: Allow and block lists
lists.sub: Senders that always get through, or never. Per mailbox, per domain or for all domains.
lists.sub_customer: Senders that always get through to your mailboxes, or never.
lists.sender_hint: A domain covers every address at that domain.
lists.allow_hint: Mail from this sender skips the spam check. Viruses and dangerous attachments are still stopped.
lists.block_hint: Mail from this sender is refused; the sender gets an error message.
lists.added_allow: {{sender}} is now always allowed. This takes effect within a minute.
lists.added_block: {{sender}} is now blocked. This takes effect within a minute.
lists.empty: No senders on the lists yet.

qreport.title: Quarantine report
qreport.sub: A daily e-mail to each recipient with the mail held for them, with a button per message to release it.
qreport.enabled_hint: Off by default. Send yourself an example first.
qreport.language_hint: Recipients have no account, so one language for everyone.
qreport.only_new: Only when there is new mail in quarantine
qreport.only_new_hint: Nobody gets the same list twice.
qreport.off_globally: The report is switched off for everyone; turn it on under When.
qreport.how_1: Each recipient gets one e-mail a day while mail is held for them, sent through the E-mail sending settings.

report.sub: This message for {{recipient}} was held because it looks like spam or is unsafe.
report.subject: Subject

report.release_allow: Release and always allow this sender

report.done_release_d: The message is on its way to {{recipient}}.
report.done_release_allow: Released, and the sender is allowed
report.done_release_allow_d: The message is on its way, and mail from {{sender}} to {{recipient}} is no longer held as spam.

report.ask_admin: Ask your administrator if you are missing an e-mail.

cluster.title: Cluster
cluster.sub: Several Mailfilter servers with the same configuration. Each one keeps filtering mail on its own if another fails.
cluster.single: This server runs on its own. Nothing changes until you create or join a cluster.
cluster.create_title: Start a cluster with this server
cluster.create_d: This server becomes the first node. Its domains, relay access, users and DKIM keys become the cluster's configuration. You then add other servers with a join code.
cluster.node_name_d: For example mailfilter01. Letters, digits, dots, dashes.
cluster.join_d: On a server that is already in the cluster, open Cluster › Add a server and copy the join code. Paste it here.
cluster.join_code_d: Starts with MFC1. Treat it like a password.
cluster.join_warn: The configuration of this server (domains, relay access, throttling, users, custom rules, e-mail sending and DKIM keys) is replaced by the cluster's. Mail queues, quarantine and the mail trace stay as they are. You log in with your cluster account afterwards.
cluster.join_sure: I understand that this server takes over the cluster's configuration
cluster.joined: This server is now part of the cluster
cluster.add_1: Install Mailfilter on the new server with the installer, as usual.
cluster.add_2: Log in on the new server and open System › Cluster.
cluster.add_3: Paste this join code under "Join an existing cluster".
cluster.code_secret: Anyone with this code can join the cluster. Do not share it.
cluster.auto_sync: Automatic, every minute and after every change
cluster.remove_d: Use this for a server that is gone for good. The other nodes stop talking to it and get a new cluster secret, so it cannot connect again. The server itself keeps its configuration. To add it again later, use a new join code.
cluster.leave_title: Take this server out of the cluster?
cluster.leave_d: This server keeps its current configuration and continues on its own. The other nodes are told and continue without it.
cluster.left: This server now runs on its own
cluster.alone: There are no other servers in this cluster yet. Use "Add a server" to add one.
cluster.versions_differ: Not every server runs the same Mailfilter version. Update all servers (Info button) so they keep syncing correctly.
cluster.import_failed: The last configuration from {{from}} ({{when}}) could not be applied on this server, so it kept its previous configuration.
cluster.dns_hint: In DNS: the shared SPF record {{spf}} lists the addresses of all servers (publish it again in the DNS toolbox after adding a server), and give each domain an MX record for every server (DNS toolbox › MX) so mail keeps arriving when one is down.
cluster.synced_d: A change on any server is sent to the others within seconds.
cluster.sync_domains: Domains and where their mail is delivered
cluster.sync_relay: Relay access: IP addresses and extra relay ports
cluster.sync_throttling: Throttling, address routes and TLS rules

sfb.how_m365_intro: The easiest way: everyone gets a Report button in Outlook on Windows, Mac, the web, iPhone and Android, and only has to press it. Set it up once per Microsoft 365 tenant.
how_m365_steps: In the Exchange admin center, add a shared mailbox for reports, for example reportspam@yourdomain.

Forward everything that arrives in that mailbox to {{spam}} (the mailbox > Mail flow settings > Email forwarding). If Microsoft blocks forwarding, allow automatic forwarding for this mailbox in the outbound anti-spam policy.

In the Microsoft Defender portal, go to Settings > Email & collaboration > User reported settings. Turn on the Report button in Outlook and send reported messages to "My reporting mailbox only": the shared mailbox.
"Not junk" reports arrive with that in the subject; Mailfilter learns those as good mail by itself.
Turn on DKIM for your domain in Microsoft 365, so Mailfilter can prove a report really comes from you. Otherwise reports wait here until someone clicks Learn.
sfb.how_outlook_intro: Works in every desktop and web mail program, without any setup. Mailfilter gets the exact original.
how_outlook_steps: Outlook: More actions (…) > Forward as attachment (Ctrl+Alt+F). Thunderbird: Message > Forward As > Attachment. Gmail on the web: the three dots > Forward as attachment.
Send it to {{spam}}, or to {{ham}} for good mail that was marked as spam.
sfb.how_phone_intro: In the Outlook app, use the Report button (see Microsoft 365). Other apps, like iPhone Mail and Gmail, simply forward the message.
how_phone_steps: Open the message and tap Forward.
Send it to {{spam}} or {{ham}}. Leave the forwarded text as it is: Mailfilter finds the original by its sender and date.
Tip: save both addresses as contacts, for example "Report spam" and "Not spam", so they are quick to pick.
how_other_steps: Forwarding as attachment works best: Mailfilter gets the exact original.
A normal forward works too, as long as the lines with the sender and date of the original stay in the text.
Only mail that Mailfilter delivered to your own domain can be reported.
sfb.how_safety: Only mail that Mailfilter delivered to the reporter's domain can be reported, and the report has to come from that domain. Reports from anywhere else are listed here, but never learned.
sfb.opt_enabled_hint: Learn from reports sent to the two addresses above.
sfb.opt_require_auth: Only trust reports that are proven
sfb.opt_require_auth_hint: The report must pass DMARC, or carry a DKIM signature or SPF pass of the reporter's domain. Other reports wait here for a click on Learn.
sfb.opt_auto_block: Block the sender for the reporter
sfb.opt_auto_block_hint: A learned spam report also puts the sender on the block list of the mailbox that got it. Undo takes it off again.
sfb.opt_per_hour_hint: More reports than this are listed but not learned. 0 = no limit.
sfb.keep_hint: A copy of each reported message is kept {{days}} days, for Learn and Undo.
